title: Cohort Runway & Fallback Checklist: staged rollout + KPI waterline
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is the canonical playbook for staged cohort rollouts of product features and model updates. It combines a timeline-focused roadmap with explicit KPI waterlines (pass/fail thresholds), a minimal smoke-test checklist per cohort, and a structured fallback/rollback decision log. Aim: make outbound signals and responsibilities unambiguous so engineering, SRE, and CS can act fast during early adopter phases.

Scope:
- Applies to: hosted API feature flags, Dedicated capacity changes, and model variant rollouts (quantization, architecture upgrades).
- Not in scope: enterprise-wide migrations (those get a separate migration runbook).

High-level rollout approach (phases):
1) Canary-internal (team-only): ~1% traffic or single org sandbox. Validate infra, billing, and smoke tests.
2) Early partner cohort: 5–10 customers (opt-in), low-latency SLA not required but qualitative signal collected.
3) Open beta cohort: selectable by org tier (growth customers) with automated monitoring and gentle throttling.
4) General availability (GA) ramp: progressive traffic increase with autoscale policies and cost-visibility gating.

KPI waterlines (primary signals used to gate forward/back):
- Latency: p95 tail latency for sample requests must remain below the waterline for the cohort to proceed. Waterline values: internal canary p95 < 120ms; Early partner p95 < 180ms; Open beta p95 < 250ms; GA p95 < 300ms.
- Error rate: 5xx or infra-level request failures must remain below 0.5% for canary, 1% for early partner, 2% for open beta.
- Quality regressions: automated eval set pass rate (per-prompt metric) must not drop more than 1.5 percentage points vs baseline.
- Cost per 100k requests: increase vs baseline must be < 20% for canary/partner, < 35% for open beta.
- Adoption / Usage: daily active orgs in cohort should meet minimal signal (canary: 1 org generating >50 requests/day; partner: median 200 req/day).

Secondary signals (contextual):
- KV cache hit ratio changes (>5% delta triggers investigation).
- Batch size and queueing depth increases >15% (possible throughput constraint).
- Tracing span increases and error budget burn rate on model-serving cluster.

Per-cohort minimal checklist (to be completed and signed off in sequence):
- Pre-roll checklist (owner: product-ops):
  - Confirm config: feature flag targeting and default fallbacks.
  - Benchmarks: dockerized micro-benchmarks for the model variant (latency/cost).
  - Infra: autoscale policies reviewed by infra and SRE.
  - Observability: dashboards, alert thresholds, and runbook links exist.
  - Communication: affected teams (SRE, support, sales) informed with schedule + contact matrix.

- Canary run (owner: eng-release):
  - Smoke tests: 10 synthetic test flows (happy path, long context, expected error types).
  - Billing sanity: confirm usage tagging and cost attrib for test traffic.
  - Data governance: verify that example request logs are anonymized for partner visibility.
  - Validation: automated eval suite run and scorecard generated.
  - Signoff: engineering lead + SRE + product-ops must approve to proceed.

- Partner cohort (owner: solutions-eng):
  - Onboard partners with template onboarding playbook.
  - Daily health recap for first 3 days (latency, errors, top failing prompts).
  - Capture qualitative feedback in shared doc (structured fields: prompt, response, issue type, severity).
  - If any waterline breach occurs, pause ramp and escalate to triage.

Rollback and fallback strategies (priority order):
1) Feature-flag flip: immediately route affected traffic to previous model variant.
2) Regional routing: shift cohort traffic to a different region with spare capacity.
3) Throttle: reduce concurrency or per-org rate limits for the cohort to reduce load.
4) Emergency revert: redeploy last-known-good serving image and invalidate caches as needed.

Decision triggers for rollback (examples):
- Sustained p95 above cohort waterline for 15 minutes and corrective measures do not reduce it.
- Error rate > 4x baseline for > 5 minutes.
- Quality metric drop > 3 percentage points on non-noisy eval suite.
- Unexpected cost delta (>2x forecast) that cannot be explained by traffic profile.

Communication play (who talks to whom):
- SRE on-call -> Slack #prodops-alerts immediate.
- Eng-release -> @product-ops lead and incident channel with brief (what, where, initial impact).
- Solutions-eng -> partner contacts with templated message (apology, mitigation, ETA).
- Exec updates: product exec thread if cohort includes enterprise customers or if incident meets P1 criteria.

Rollout schedule template (example):
- Week 0: Pre-roll validation, bench runs, signoffs.
- Week 1: Canary-internal (48–72 hours).
- Week 2: Partner cohort (pilot window: 7–14 days).
- Week 3: Open beta (monitor for 14 days).
- Week 4+: GA ramp if all gates clear.
Adjust window lengths for model-level changes: major architecture changes require longer partner windows.

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Token-cost explosion on long-tail prompts. Mitigation: set per-org cost alarms, enable token caps.
- Risk: Silent quality regressions for niche prompts. Mitigation: add focused eval prompts from partner telemetry.
- Risk: Autoscaler thrash under sudden traffic. Mitigation: increase cooldowns, add buffer capacity.

Post-roll review (retro):
- Owners: product-ops + eng-release + SRE. Deliverables within 7 days: incident log (if any), KPI delta report, lessons learned, one-sentence change to rollout playbook.

Appendix: quick smoke test checklist (copyable for runbooks)
- 5x sample happy-path prompts -> verify expected completions.
- 3x long-context prompts (2–4x usual length) -> verify p95 not degraded.
- 2x failure-mode prompts (malformed, rate-limit exceed) -> verify graceful error.
- 1x quantization check (if deploying quantized model): compare output parity on 8 canonical prompts.

Notes and open questions (work-in-progress):
- How to encode partner qualitative feedback into automated eval triggers? (action: product-ops + applied-ml to prototype mapping by 2024-10-05).
- Template for cost forecasting per-cohort (action: finance + product-ops to produce a one-page template).

Status: in_review. Please add comments inline with concrete numbers if you own a signal in the KPI table.
